findings.title: HKMA and Swift continue collaboration on Project Ensemble and Swift ledger

rendered_html: 📔 Regulatory Bulletin — 17 November 2026 (Daily) Executive Summary • 🟡 HKMA and Swift are expanding exploratory work on multi-currency tokenised-deposit interoperability, relevant to strategic decisions on cross-border payment and digital-product infrastructure. • The collaboration is not a participation mandate, supervisory expectation or production timetable; no source deadline is stated. • Banks choosing to explore the use case may need to assess settlement, resilience, data, third-party and cross-border legal dependencies before committing scope. Hong Kong 🟡 HKMA and Swift continue collaboration on Project Ensemble and Swift ledger 🇭🇰 Item ID: item-20261116-hkma-press-17c87bd67d ⏰ Deadline: No source deadline stated Products: Payments; Digital; Cross-border/GBA The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) announced a strengthened collaboration with Swift to explore cross-border, multi-currency tokenised-deposit interoperability between the Swift ledger and Project Ensemble’s settlement layer. HKMA named Bank of China (Hong Kong), Standard Chartered Bank (Hong Kong) and HSBC in the collaboration and said the work aims to support real-time, always-on and programmable transactions. This is a market-development update, not a rule, consultation, participation mandate or supervisory expectation, and the release does not evidence production deployment. Banks considering these use cases may need to assess entity and booking location, customer use case, settlement, data, resilience, and Swift/Project Ensemble dependencies before deciding whether to explore them. Source: HKMA and Swift continue the collaboration to explore cross-border payment interoperability through Project Ensemble and Swift ledger SG/UK/GLOBAL Benchmark Comparable overseas developments and commercial/control benchmarks. They do not establish Hong Kong requirements. Watch List • Monitor whether participating institutions or the collaboration publish production use cases, participation terms or implementation milestones.
